summary: BBC on Ahramat branch: 64km long, 200-700m wide, bordered 31 pyramids; suggests Egyptians used river's energy to carry heavy blocks rather than human labor.
content: Research team from University of North Carolina Wilmington discovered the Ahramat branch, a long-lost ancient branch of the Nile, now hidden under desert and farmland. It was roughly 64km (39 miles) long and 200-700m wide, bordering 31 pyramids built between 4,700 and 3,700 years ago. Co-author Dr Suzanne Onstine: ancient Egyptians could 'use the river's energy to carry these heavy blocks, rather than human labour - it's just a lot less effort'.
